spans.label: new(): ordered circuit construction
spans.note: Dependency-ordered build plan; the externally supplied `single_withdrawal_vd` is a parameter, not a produced artifact.

spans.label: the three verifier-data accessors
spans.note: Only the chain verifier data is modeled, as the cyclic key passed to the step circuit; the step and withdrawal accessors return opaque plonky2 handles.

spans.label: prove_step(): step circuit then chain wrapper
spans.note: Call order and error precedence are modeled; proving is an opaque callback.

spans.label: prove_final(): binds the prover address and ext public state
spans.note: Exactly one call: the chain proof it is handed is NOT natively verified and the extended public state is not re-derived.

boundaries.name: plonky2-proving-and-verification
boundaries.obligation: Every `prove` and `verify` call is an opaque callback returning success or failure; nothing in the model implies proof soundness, completeness, zero-knowledge, or recursive-verification soundness.

boundaries.name: circuit-construction-lowering
boundaries.obligation: `generate_cd`, each circuit's `new`, and `verifier_data()` lower to plonky2 gates that the model does not represent; the build plan records dependency order only.

boundaries.name: withdrawal-cyclic-verifier-key
boundaries.obligation: The model records that the withdrawal chain verifier data is passed into the step circuit, but does not prove it equals the key inside a chained proof.

boundaries.name: single-withdrawal-verifier-key
boundaries.obligation: `single_withdrawal_vd` is supplied by the caller; the model does not check it is the key of the real single-withdrawal circuit.

boundaries.name: withdrawal-prover-binding
boundaries.obligation: The prover address and extended public state are threaded into an opaque circuit call; no claim is made that the resulting proof binds them.
